newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen mixed to higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen mixed to higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street was expected to open mixed to slightly higher on Thursday, riding a wave of positive momentum after the Dow industrials powered past the 8,000-point mark yesterday, but subject to mild profit-taking.
Stocks could face some profit-taking after the Dow Jones Industrial average closed up 63 points at 8039, analysts said.
But a steady stream of corporate earnings, including results from several Dow components and Microsoft Corp, could then provide fresh impetus to move higher.

"The momentum is there and the earnings reports have been good," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said. "We should go higher even from a technical standpoint. As we approach options expiry tomorrow, that should fuel the markets' upward momentum."
Both bonds and stocks will also watch the housing starts data for June, due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. They were forecast at 1.45 million, compared with 1.397 million in May.
"Right now we look set to open a little mixed to higher," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said. "But the housing figures could intervene."

In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index rose 0.70 points to 943.00. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond, which pierced resistance to break through a key 6.50 percent yield yesterday, was flat at 6.48 percent.
U.S. stocks edged lower in London trading on Thursday, with investors taking profits after yesterday's surge.
Nasdaq posted its biggest single-day point rise yesterday, gaining 38.5 to 1,581.
Today, the Dow will face results from components Gillette Co, Merck & Co, Coca-Cola Co and McDonalds Corp.
U.S. drug maker Merck posted second quarter earnings of $0.96 per share compared with $0.80 per share in the year-ago quarter, on revenues of $5.91 billion.

Among other Dow stocks, AT&T Corp shares eased slightly in London after news that its president, John Walter, had resigned nearly nine months after he was chosen as the heir apparent to chief executive Robert Allen.
Giant technology company Microsoft Corp was also set to report fourth quarter earnings. The First Call consensus estimate was $0.79 per share versus $0.43 in the year-ago fourth quarter.
The dollar mainted its gains against the yen, trading at 116.10/20 yen in Tokyo. In Europe, the dollar was steady at around 1.7944/54 marks.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 160.51 points, or 0.79 percent, at 20,519.25.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 16.4 at 4947.8.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that with the Dow Jones Industrial average topping new highs, some bullish Wall Street strategists have turned bearish on the U.S. stock market.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that the Dow Jones Industrial average has surged, as investors keep pouring money into the stock market.
